area: Forest pond near Lake Kuchnia / Olszowka-Gardeja study area, Poland

hydrology_investigation.priority: Trace the pond and Lake Kuchnia through verified main channels, side tributaries, inflows, outflows, ditches, culverts and water-management structures before assigning a cause.
hydrology_investigation.candidate_chain_status: public description pending official geometry, elevation and flow-direction verification
required_checks: Load official Hydroportal or equivalent public hydrography for the AOI.
Build a directed graph of the main river, tributaries, lake inlets, lake outlets, ditches, culverts and control structures.
Use DEM profiles only as flow-direction context and verify low-relief areas in the field.
Compare matched-season water extent across years with sensor harmonization and uncertainty.
Check discharge or stage upstream and downstream together with precipitation, evapotranspiration, groundwater and soil moisture.
Inspect suspected restrictions or damaged drainage structures in the field before assigning causation.

limitations: The satellite record supports a state change of the historically persistent visible pond footprint, not a published exact 2026 open-water area or loss percentage.
The visible state change does not establish whether inflow loss, outflow change, obstruction, groundwater, precipitation, evapotranspiration, vegetation or another process caused it.
Training metrics and optimization losses are not environmental ground truth.
Official hydrological geometry, field measurements and independently verified infrastructure records are still required.
